The test `testMissingRequiredOptions` is checking for a `MissingOptionException` to be thrown when parsing command line arguments with a missing required option. The test expects the exception message to be specific about the missing required options.

The current bug report mentions that the `MissingOptionException.getMessage()` string has changed from CLI 1.0 to 1.1, becoming almost unreadable in CLI 1.1. The report suggests changing a method to address this issue.

By looking at the implementation of the `parse` method in `org.apache.commons.cli.Parser`, we can see that it is responsible for parsing the command line arguments with the given `Options`. The `Options` are created using `OptionBuilder.create(char)`.

The issue seems to be related to the formatting of the exception message in the `MissingOptionException` in a newer version of the CLI library. The change in formatting might be causing the test to fail when comparing the expected exception message. To address this issue, the method that constructs the exception message or the way it is formatted needs to be adjusted in the code.

Next, I will suggest the best locations to fix this issue.
